Cc: ops@brightwave.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: AZ-3 elevated latency / 5xx spike impacting BrightWave storefront

Team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-user latency and 5xx responses at ~08:30 PDT that correlates to requests routed through your AZ-3 (us-west-3). Page loads are timing out for ~17% of our sessions and throughput has dropped by roughly 30% since the spike. Our ops team temporarily shifted traffic to US-EAST but that is filling up our capacity and affecting checkout throughput.

Attached are our request-rate and p95 latency charts for the last 3 hours (az3-metrics-20270528.pdf). This is customer-impacting — we need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA, and we need to understand whether this is an ongoing risk for the rest of the day. Please escalate to your engineering leadership and let us know the next steps.

We expect daily peak traffic at 11:00 PDT and cannot absorb continued errors through that window.

Sarah
Sarah Holt
CTO (acting), BrightWave Retail

Team — quick technical status and immediate plan:

Initial triage (09:30–10:45):
- Telemetry shows elevated packet loss at the AZ-3 network fabric layer and a concurrent increase in model server replica restart rate (LROs) in the us-west-3 pool.
- KV-cache miss rates jumped ~12% leading to extra token-generation work and downstream latency amplification.

Immediate remediation (in flight):
1) Activate traffic-steering policy to prefer us-west-2 for BrightWave traffic and drain AZ-3 nodes for safe reprovisioning (will take ~12–18 minutes to steer & stabilize).
2) Increase instance pool in us-west-2 by +25% from burst capacity; pre-warm model caches for BrightWave model variants (expected impact 20–30 minutes).
3) Temporarily raise retry budget on the client-side routing rule for BrightWave to reduce observed 5xx amplification while we drain failing replicas.

Expected ETA: 20–35 minutes for visible p95 improvement; 45–60 minutes for full recovery. If steering is blocked by BrightWave or regulatory constraints, we'll provide a mitigation plan for staged fallback with conservative concurrency limits.

Longer-term suspicion: an intermittent NIC firmware regression on a subset of AZ-3 hosts combined with a storage controller GC pattern under high sustained throughput. We will capture traces and a post-incident RCA.

Subject: Board alert: AZ-3 degradation — status update and next steps

Sarah — summary for BrightWave and Redwood execs below. Please accept my apologies for the disruption and thank you for the quick coordination.

Timeline:
- 08:30 PDT: BrightWave reports p95 latency and 5xx spike for AZ-3.
- 09:20 PDT: Redwood engaged; incident bridge opened.
- 11:00 PDT: Engineering steered traffic to us-west-2 and pre-warmed additional model caches.
- 12:10 PDT: Observed p95 improvement of ~55% relative to the spike baseline. Full stabilization achieved by ~13:00 PDT.

What we did:
- Activated a cross-region steering policy to reduce load on the affected AZ-3 pool.
- Reprovisioned and drained impacted AZ-3 instances for safety; engineering captured trace data for RCA.
- Offered BrightWave a temporary increase in burst capacity at no charge while we complete the RCA.

Open items and asks:
- Exec decision on a customer-facing SLA credit. Ben and I recommend pre-authorizing a one-time partial credit tied to the duration of elevated errors; we'll finalize numbers with finance.
- Engineering to provide RCA draft within 72 hours; we will share remediation timelines for firmware/host replacement.
- Ops to run a cross-account capacity runbook to ensure spillover capacity for peak windows.

Sarah, are you available for a brief 20-minute post-mortem with our leadership at 17:00 PDT today? We want to review the impact, the mitigation, and next steps for resilience.

Thanks again for patience — we take incidents like this seriously and will follow up with RCA and compensation details.

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
